messages.subject: Multilevel path analyses
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm trying to help out some colleagues of mine. One part of their 
dataset consists of about 200 students in 20 classes whose L1 and L2 
skills were measured at three points in time. The primary research 
question is whether skills learnt in one language transfer to the other 
language.

I've taken a closer look at some studies on similar topics, and they 
tend to tackle this question by means of path analysis/structural 
equation modelling. The general idea would then be to compare the 
structural model

L1.1 -> L1.2 -> L1.3
L2.1 -> L2.2 -> L2.3

to models with causal links between L1.1 -> L2.2, L2.1 -> L1.2, and 
similarly for T2 and T3.

I have some inkling about path analysis/SEM, so running a similar 
analysis (and, not unimportant, explaining it) would be feasible. (The 
data I have at present don't require the specification of latent 
variables, though parallel datasets might.) But surely, the hierarchical 
dependencies (students in classes) need to be accounted for, too?

I took a look at a couple of articles on multilevel SEM, but I couldn't 
make much sense out of them; what little applied examples they showed 
were MPlus etc. based.

So, assuming that the hierarchy in the data needs to be specified in 
this kind of analysis, too, does anyone have any pointers as to how one 
could go about doing so? Examples in R would be much appreciated. 
Alternative approaches, i.e. other than path analysis, would do, too.

Thanks!
Jan

messages.subject: Re: Multilevel path analyses
messages.body_plain:
I think I might have found a possible solution. Let me know what you 
think :)

My proposed solution would be to reorganise the data as follows (see 
attachment). Rather than force a multilevel structure on a path model, 
I'd force a path structure on a multilevel model. To this end, the 
students' L1 and L2 scores at the two last measurement points are 
entered into a column featuring the dependent variable. The other 
columns identify what language (L1/L2) the score is for and at what time 
(2 or 3) it was measured. Other columns contain the main predictor 
variables, i.e. the L1 and L2 scores at the previous point in time 
(SameMinus1 / OtherMinus1).

Student    Class    LanguageTested    Time    SameMinus1 OtherMinus1    
Score
A    C1    L1    2    14    12    20
A    C1    L2    2    12    14    15
A    C1    L1    3    20    15    23
A    C1    L2    3    15    20    18
B    C1    L1    2    4    2    8
B    C1    L2    2    2    4    6
B    C1    L1    3    8    6    12
B    C1    L2    3    6    8    11

Then, I should be able to fit a model like:

lmer(Score ~ Time*LanguageTested*SameMinus1 + 
Time*LanguageTested*OtherMinus1 + (1|Class) + (1|Student))

Would that work, you think?
